A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeSpot. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material relocated or resized in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, calibration and error analyses, and supervised fine-tuning results, including Table 3, Figure 4, and Appendices D–H.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds model evaluations and joint-training experiments. These establish original empirical content independently of ambiguities in the new human comparison.

M1.justification: v1 fine-tunes country and time prediction separately. v2 adds simultaneous country-and-time fine-tuning with shared LoRA parameters in Appendix H.2. This extends the training objective while retaining the base architecture, benchmark pipeline, and existing single-task procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,455-image benchmark and geographic and temporal prediction tasks. New human and joint-training comparisons reuse this coverage. Table 2 changes the country count from 82 to 80, agreeing with both abstracts; the PDFs do not establish an underlying coverage change.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains all 23 earlier VLM comparators and adds GPT-5.2, Qwen3-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-32B-Instruct, and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct. It also introduces undergraduate and expert human comparison groups, detailed in Table 25, substantially broadening the comparison framework.

E3.justification: v2 adds complementary-task checkpoint evaluation and five-epoch joint training using the existing LoRA configuration and 40%/60% split. Appendix J additionally describes a new image-only human evaluation with three undergraduates and three experts completing the benchmark under the existing metrics. Original benchmark metrics and splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices H.1.3 and H.2 test whether single-task adaptation harms the other task and whether joint training mitigates that interference, using Tables 21–24 and learning curves. Figure 3 replaces a Spanish night example with a Russian morning example; the earlier Italian coastal-walkway appendix case is removed.

E5.justification: v1 already specifies fixed training seeds and reports rank-correlation significance tests. v2 additionally reports three joint-SFT runs differing in data ordering, with individual trajectories and averages in Table 23 and Figures 10–11. This is new stability reporting, not evidence that earlier evaluations were rerun.

E6.justification: All original Table 3 model values and Figure 4 single-task curves are retained. Added results include four VLM rows, human scores, cross-task degradation, and joint-SFT epoch-five averages of 15.72% country and 22.36% time accuracy. Qualitative case entries also change, and Table 2 revises 82 countries to 80.

T1.justification: The task formulation, calibration and evaluation equations in Appendix D, and rank-stability definitions in Appendix G are unchanged. The new gradient-conflict discussion is conceptual interpretation, without added formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a joint geo-temporal benchmark, weak temporal grounding and consistency in current VLMs, and improvements from SFT that remain insufficient. The added experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds extensive explanations attributing cross-task interference to competing illumination sensitivities and shared LoRA gradients, alongside human-versus-model interpretations and new training recommendations. Some interpretations overreach: the asserted expert advantage across all temporal fields conflicts with expert month accuracy of 46.06% versus o4-mini's 48.20% in Table 3.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses three primary and two senior annotators, annotation effort, OpenRouter usage, approximately USD 1,450 inference cost, and estimated token consumption. It also specifies reuse of existing settings for joint training. Earlier LoRA hyperparameters, prompts, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Buschoff et al., Binz et al., and Chen et al. to contextualize SFT limitations and alternative training directions, while removing the Li et al. (2026) and Zhou et al. (2025) references. The benchmark's positioning against existing geolocation and multimodal benchmarks remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the temporal-motivation passage, rewrites the main SFT discussion, adds subsection and appendix organization for the new studies, and makes small wording corrections. Publication information and a conflict-of-interest disclosure are added. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 3, adds Tables 21–25 and Figures 10–11, revises Figure 3, and clarifies Table 4's caption. The map moves into a single column, and most retained appendix examples are reduced from one to two panels per page. These constitute substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparisons, repeated-run joint-training diagnostics, and reproducibility disclosures. However, Appendix J describes a completed human study while Table 25 labels its scores 'Projected Human Baselines,' leaving an important addition's status unclear. Its claim of expert superiority across all temporal fields also contradicts the reported month scores. These unresolved evidence and interpretation issues prevent a confident net quality judgment despite the useful additions.
